title: Solymosi–Stojaković lower bound on four-point lines: n^{2−O(1/√log n)} construction

problemStatement.formal: Solymosi & Stojaković (2013): for every $\varepsilon > 0$, there is $N$ such that for all $n \geq N$, there exists a planar point set $P$ with $|P| = n$, NoFiveCollinear $P$, and $\mathrm{fourPointLineCount}(P) \geq n^{2 - \varepsilon / \sqrt{\log n}}$. The construction uses random linear projections of a high-dimensional grid: a $d$-dimensional grid $G_d = \{0, \ldots, k-1\}^d$ has many 4-term arithmetic progressions; a generic linear $\pi : \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}^2$ projects these APs to 4-collinear sets while (with positive probability over $\pi$) creating no 5 collinear points. Parameter optimization in $d, k$ yields the $n^{2 - O(1/\sqrt{\log n})}$ rate.
problemStatement.plain: Erdős Problem #101 ($100) asks for the asymptotic behavior of L_4(n) = max |{four-point lines}| over n-point sets with no five collinear. The parent formalizes the upper bound L_4(n) ≤ n(n-1)/12. This OQ-04 targets the formalization of the Solymosi–Stojaković (2013) lower bound L_4(n) ≥ n^{2−O(1/√log n)}, which disproved Erdős's conjectured Θ(n^{3/2}) shape. Sandwiches the truth between n^{2−o(1)} and n^2 — the remaining gap is the open o(n^2) question.
whyMatters: Provides a machine-verified lower bound complementing the parent's machine-verified upper bound — a quantitative sandwich for an Erdős problem ($100 unsolved $o(n^2)$ gap).
Solymosi–Stojaković's bound disproved Erdős's $\Theta(n^{3/2})$ conjecture. Formalizing it documents a refuted classical conjecture in Lean — historically significant in its own right.
The random-perturbation incidence-geometry technique generalizes: Behrend-style AP_4 lower bounds, Szemerédi cases, sum-product lower bounds, all use related polynomial-genericity arguments.

Demonstrates that Mathlib's measure theory + probability + discrete geometry layers can carry a real combinatorial-geometry theorem — a stress test for the gallery's combinatorial / probabilistic infrastructure.

proven: Solymosi & Stojaković (2013), *Combinatorica* 33: 247–258 — proved $L_4(n) \geq n^{2 - O(1/\sqrt{\log n})}$ via random projection of a high-dimensional grid. Modern reference: Brass–Moser–Pach (2005) §7.2.

Parent gallery `Proofs/Erdos101Problem.lean` (757 lines, 23 theorems, 0 axioms, 0 sorries, status: verified) provides PlanarPointSet / collinear / NoFiveCollinear / fourPointLineCount / improved_upper_bound (≤ n(n-1)/12).
Grünbaum (1972), *Arrangements and Spreads* — weaker lower bound $L_4(n) \gtrsim n^{3/2}$ via specific construction; pre-Solymosi–Stojaković state of art.

The Polynomial.eval_ne_zero infrastructure for non-vanishing arguments exists but the genericity-of-projection step may need new lemmas.

UPDATE (researcher-6, 2026-07-12): opened the DIOPHANTINE/rational layer of the four-point-line conic Q=p²+q²+r²+pq+qr+rp=5 in NEW companion Proofs/Erdos101OQ04Rational.lean (0-axiom, 0-sorry, docker-verified Lean v4.26.0, 3063 jobs). Added ternary_conic_secant — a division-free secant parametrization: from any rational base point on Q=5 and any rational direction, τ·Q_d=−N yields a new rational conic point (identity Q(P₀+τd)=Q(P₀)+τN+τ²Q_d). Since Q=5 carries the rational point (−8/3,1/3,1), this exhibits it as rationally parametrized ⇒ infinitely many rational four-point lines on the quartic. Demonstrated by producing a SECOND explicit oblique rational four-point line (−7/3,2,−1/3,2/3) via a concrete secant (base (−1,2,1), dir (1,0,1), τ=−4/3), proven collinear on the quartic, genuinely oblique (abscissa set not negation-closed) and distinct from the iter-12 witness. SCOPE: arithmetic-structure layer only — does NOT touch the OPEN solymosi_stojakovic_lower_bound (line 358, deep n^{2−o(1)} random-projection construction); the quartic route caps at Ω(n). The rational parametrization is the mechanism any explicit rational/integer super-linear construction would build on. Prior summary below.

UPDATE (researcher-2, 2026-07-12): added the common-line⟺fixed-sphere bridge (collinear_anchored_pair_iff_common_line + four_onQuartic_onLine_iff_sq, Erdos101OQ04.lean:3043/3086) — converts the determinant `collinear` predicate into an explicit affine line y=m·x+e and proves four onQuartic points are collinear ⟺ their abscissae lie on the FIXED 2-sphere {Σx=0, Σx²=10}. 0-axiom, 0-new-sorry, docker-verified (Lean v4.26.0). File 3470→3536 lines. The tractable arithmetic layer is now essentially complete (sphere/ternary-conic reductions + oblique-quadruple engine quartic_fourPointLineCount_from_quadruples + linear floor L₄(n)≥n/4 all present). SINGLE remaining OPEN sorry = solymosi_stojakovic_lower_bound (line 358), the deep n^{2−o(1)} super-linear construction. EXACT GAP (crisp, artifact-only): exhibit, for arbitrarily large n, a set A⊂ℝ of size n with super-linearly many 4-subsets {a,b,c,d} each satisfying Σ=0 ∧ Σsq=10 (all on the fixed sphere) — a rigid additive/sphere-energy problem, genuinely multi-session; the symmetric construction is provably disjoint (linear ceiling), so oblique/concurrent quadruples are required.
insights: Parent upper bound fourPointLineCount<=n(n-1)/12 is verified; the gap to a proven lower bound is the open content.

The bare Grunbaum parabola has NO four-point lines (PROVEN no-three-collinear): it is the general-position BASE the lower-bound construction is built on top of, not itself the four-point-line witness — and it is now realized as an explicit ℝ² PlanarPointSet (realParabolaSet) of size p satisfying NoFiveCollinear with 0 axioms.

ZMod p general position TRANSFERS to ℝ² general position via the canonical-representative embed (i,j)↦(i.val,j.val): three lifted points collinear in ℝ² means an INTEGER 2x2 determinant vanishes (coords are integers in {0,…,p-1}), and 0 in ℤ reduces to 0 in ZMod p — so a ZMod p arc lifts to a real arc. Clean ℝ→ℤ→ZMod p cast chain (exact_mod_cast for ℝ→ℤ, then push_cast + ZMod.natCast_zmod_val for ℤ→ZMod p). REUSABLE for any ZMod p point construction.
A nonzero quadratic over any Field has <=2 roots via an elementary divided-difference argument (no_three_quadratic_roots): (i-j)(a(i+j)+b)=0 twice + subtract => a=0 => b=0. Reusable, Polynomial-free.
The 2 remaining sorries (Grunbaum Omega(n^{3/2}) COUNT, Solymosi-Stojakovic) require the full sumset/grid + random-perturbation construction over the now-realized general-position ℝ² base.

The 4x4 grid is the MAXIMAL no-five-collinear grid: 5 distinct x OR 5 distinct y in a grid would give a vertical/horizontal 5-collinear line, so both dimensions cap at 4. Within that cap it still realizes 10 four-point lines (4 rows+4 cols+2 diagonals), lines in general position (no common point) — the right micro-model for the Solymosi-Stojakovic grid projection.

Lean gotcha: Finset.card_product is stated for the SProd notation `s xs t` (SProd.sprod); if a set is defined via `Finset.product` (the .product method) rw [Finset.card_product] fails to match syntactically even though the two are defeq — bridge with `rw [show s.product t = s xs t from rfl, Finset.card_product]`. mem_product still unifies through .mp (defeq), only rw needs the syntactic bridge.

ENGINE (researcher-5, 2026-07-11): the count has a matching trivial UPPER cap fourPointLineCount ≤ C(n,4) — the defining powerset-filter drops into the 4-uniform layer Finset.powersetCard 4 P.points (via ← Finset.card_powersetCard, then card_le_card weakening the collinearity clause). And the ge_of_injOn_family / ge_of_subset engines fold cleanly into IsLowerBoundConstruction one-shot constructors (isLowerBoundConstruction_of_injOn_family / _of_family), which is the exact shape every explicit witness (crossSet/asteriskSet/gridSet) produces — future witnesses skip the Nat.cast/fourPointLineCount boilerplate.

EVERY four-point line on the quartic has its four abscissae on a SINGLE FIXED 2-sphere {Σx=0, Σx²=10}⊂ℝ⁴, independent of the line's slope/intercept (Vieta: the monic quartic x⁴−5x²−mx−e always has e₁=0, e₂=−5 as its x³- and x²-coefficients, giving Σx=0 and Σx²=(Σx)²−2e₂=10 for ANY m,e). The RIGIDITY of this fixed sphere (no scaling freedom — the constant 10 is pinned by the quartic) is the structural reason the linear floor is hard to beat: super-linear count needs super-linearly many distinct 4-subsets of an n-set all landing on ONE fixed sphere, i.e. genuine additive structure (Solymosi-Stojaković), not a scaling trick.

Symmetric quadruples {t,−t,s,−s} (t²+s²=5) that power quartic_linear_lower_bound give PAIRWISE-DISJOINT four-point lines: two distinct symmetric quadruples share a coordinate only if they share t or s, which forces the same set. So the linear construction never exhibits two four-point lines through a common vertex — CONCURRENCY (a point on ≥2 four-point lines) is the qualitative prerequisite for super-linearity and requires OBLIQUE quadruples (e.g. {0,2,−1+√2,−1−√2}: Σ=0, Σsq=10, not closed under negation).

A candidate SS construction is only specified up to a plane similarity (choice of origin + scale); similarity invariance (translatePlane/scalePlane preserve NoFiveCollinear and fourPointLineCount exactly) lets a future construction PR normalise its witness without re-proving the framework conditions — e.g. move freely between the fixed spheres Σx²=c.

The four-point-line conic Q=5 carries the rational point (−8/3,1/3,1); a conic with one rational point is rationally parametrized, so it has a DENSE (hence infinite) set of rational points — infinitely many rational four-point lines lie on the quartic y=x⁴−5x². The secant lemma ternary_conic_secant makes this constructive (division-free, ring-valid).

Distinct-line WARNING for the additive count: the earlier symmetric integer point (−1,2,1) yields the SYMMETRIC quadruple {−2,−1,1,2} (=(2,−2,1,−1)), NOT a new oblique family; a secant step away from it is required to reach genuine oblique points like (−7/3,2,−1/3).

First converts the signed-area determinant predicate `collinear` into an EXPLICIT affine line y=m·x+e (slope m=(b.2−a.2)/(b.1−a.1), intercept e=a.2−m·a.1; purely planar, no onQuartic), then chains with four_onQuartic_collinear_iff_sq to prove: four onQuartic points with distinct abscissae lie on one line ⟺ Σx=0 ∧ Σx²=10. 0-axiom, 0-new-sorry, docker-build verified (Lean v4.26.0, only the pre-existing OPEN sorry@358 remains). Reusable API for any SS-style construction that names the line (slope/intercept) through a four-point line rather than the determinant.

PlaneAut + map_noFiveCollinear/map_fourPointLineCount/map_isLowerBoundConstruction + translatePlane/scalePlane (Erdos101OQ04Similarity.lean, researcher-5): SIMILARITY INVARIANCE of the lower-bound framework. A PlaneAut is a collinearity-preserving self-bijection of ℝ² with explicit two-sided inverse; its induced action S↦S.image on a PlanarPointSet preserves NoFiveCollinear (map_noFiveCollinear) and EXACTLY preserves fourPointLineCount (map_fourPointLineCount, a Finset.card_nbij bijection on collinear 4-subsets), hence IsLowerBoundConstruction transfers verbatim (map_isLowerBoundConstruction). translatePlane v and scalePlane c (c≠0) instantiate it: any construction can be recentred at the origin and rescaled (e.g. between spheres Σx²=c) without recounting. 0-axiom (propext/Classical.choice/Quot.sound), 0 sorry, lake-build verified Lean v4.26.0.

ternary_conic_secant (Erdos101OQ04Rational.lean): division-free secant/rational-parametrization lemma for the four-point-line conic Q=p²+q²+r²+pq+qr+rp=5 — from any base point on Q=5 and any direction, τ·Q_d=−N gives a new conic point; proves Q=5 is rationally parametrized (Q(P₀+τd)=Q(P₀)+τN+τ²Q_d, linear_combination)
